A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same judge-generalization study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite expanded content and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original DeepScaleR experiments with three judge backbones, multiple training recipes, continual training, and seen-versus-unseen question evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original MMLU-Pro evaluations with Ministral-8B and Mistral-24B, plus generator-level question-retention measurements.

M1.justification: The pairwise judging procedure, GPT-4o supervision, SFT/DPO/SFT+DPO objectives, backbones, and continual-training procedure are retained. Added prompt and split descriptions document the setup without establishing changes to the existing method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates mathematics through DeepScaleR. v2 adds training and evaluation on MMLU-Pro, extending coverage to knowledge-intensive multiple-choice questions across 14 domains, including humanities, social sciences, and law. Continual-training experiments remain confined to DeepScaleR.

E2.justification: The zero-shot, SFT, DPO, SFT+DPO, and existing continual-training comparisons are retained. MMLU-Pro extends the existing comparator set to another dataset; no comparator is added or removed from a corresponding DeepScaleR experiment.

E3.justification: The added MMLU-Pro experiments use 10K training samples and 10 epochs/1,500 steps, while DeepScaleR retains 70K samples and 3 epochs/2,800 steps. Both use the existing split design, consistent accuracy, and 2.5K evaluation pairs before order reversal. The newly stated matching of questions across weak/strong splits is a disclosure, not an established alteration of the earlier protocol.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix C adds a focused selection-bias diagnostic: Table 3 and Figure 9 measure question retention by generator and relate it to generator strength. This examines the consequences of requiring both correct and incorrect sampled responses. Existing continual-training and preference-strength comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The 20 generator responses per question were already specified in v1; v2 supplies sampling details without establishing additional repetitions.

E6.justification: v2 adds MMLU-Pro generator strengths and judge results, plus retention percentages for both datasets. For example, Table 4 reports MMLU-Pro strong/unseen accuracy of 52.92% versus 57.31% for weak- versus strong-trained Mistral-24B with SFT+DPO. These are newly reported comparisons; all DeepScaleR accuracy entries from v1 Table 3 are preserved in v2 Table 4.

T1.justification: The dual-distribution formulation, judge mapping, generalization metrics, and consistent-accuracy definition in Equations (1)–(10) are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the stated empirical scope from mathematics to two datasets covering multiple domains. The principal claims about future-proofing, backward compatibility, continual learning, and question generalization remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets smaller MMLU-Pro degradations as evidence of domain dependence, explains why the generator grouping is insensitive to thresholds within the observed gaps, and acknowledges a medium-difficulty selection bias from response filtering. These qualify the interpretation without replacing the central conclusions.

D1.justification: v2 adds code/data and project-page links, dataset identifiers, explicit question matching across weak/strong splits, and Appendix G with six prompt templates, temperature/sample allocations, top-p, prompt randomization, and greedy judge decoding. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the linked resources' availability is not verified by the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds the MMLU-Pro reference, Wang et al. (2024c), to support the new dataset. The existing related-work discussion and positioning relative to judge training and distribution-shift research remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes terminology and hyphenation, updates author notes and the publication header, expands setup explanations, and adds appendix contents and Sections F–G. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact, rather than undergoing extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 moves the existing DeepScaleR generator-strength plot into the main text, adds Figures 8–12 and a retention table, and redesigns the accuracy table into side-by-side dataset blocks. It also adds six boxed prompts. Captions for Figures 7 and 12 incorrectly describe weak/strong bar patterns as seen/unseen questions.

improvement.justification: The MMLU-Pro experiments substantially strengthen evidence beyond v1's mathematics-only setting. The selection-bias audit and detailed prompt, sampling, and data-construction disclosures also address important transparency and reproducibility gaps. Different training budgets limit the domain-dependence interpretation, and some new captions are misleading, but these issues do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical scope and documentation.
